intended_object: The extensive coverage on a finitary (pre)extensive category C: covering families of B are the finite families {X_a → B} for which the induced map ∐ X_a → B is an isomorphism, i.e. finite coproduct decompositions of B. Inferred from the docstring, the name and the module (coherent/extensive/regular topologies).
explanation: The coverings of B are presieves `ofArrows X π` indexed by a finite type, with `Sigma.desc π : ∐ X → B` an isomorphism. That is exactly the standard extensive coverage, whose covers are finite coproduct decompositions. `FinitaryPreExtensive` supplies the finite coproducts and makes coproducts stable under pullback. That stability is what the pullback axiom needs, so this hypothesis is the natural setting and not an extra restriction. Indexing by `α : Type` with `Finite α` loses nothing, because every finite family can be reindexed by a `Fin n`. The empty family is also handled correctly: it covers B exactly when B is initial, which matches the standard convention. Mathlib has no other, more general definition of this coverage; this declaration is Mathlib's own.
